purpose: Hydromorphone is a strong prescription pain medicine used to treat moderate to severe pain that other pain medicines cannot control well. It is often used after surgery, for cancer-related pain, or for serious injuries. Your doctor will only prescribe it when your pain truly needs a powerful treatment.
how_it_works: Hydromorphone works by attaching to special receptors in your brain and spinal cord called opioid receptors. When it connects to these receptors, it blocks pain signals from traveling through your body, so you feel less pain. Think of it like a lock and key — the medicine is the key that fits into the lock and turns off the pain alarm.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include drowsiness or feeling very sleepy, nausea or upset stomach, constipation, dizziness, and headache. Some people also feel lightheaded, especially when standing up quickly. These effects are common with opioid medicines and your care team can help manage them.
warnings: This is a very powerful medicine that can slow your breathing to a dangerous level, especially if you take too much or mix it with alcohol, sleeping pills, or anti-anxiety medicines. It can be habit-forming and lead to dependence or addiction. Never share this medicine with anyone else, keep it locked away safely, and never stop it suddenly without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor right away if you feel extremely sleepy, confused, or have trouble breathing.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very individual and depends on your pain level, your body, and whether you have taken opioids before. For adults, immediate-release tablets or liquid are often started at 2 to 4 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Extended-release tablets (Exalgo) are taken just once a day and are only for people who already take opioids regularly. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed — never take more or take it more often than directed.
